**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the clone source before dropping the target**

When `--mode clone --force` uses a source predating migration 146, this check runs only after the destination has been dropped, recreated, restored, and modified by `_post_clone_cleanup`; the advertised `RuntimeError` therefore destroys the previous slot and leaves an unusable replacement without `story_identity`. Check the source for this table before disposing or dropping the target so this known incompatibility fails before any destructive operation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in f192fccd. Both identity tables and the optional singleton UUID are now checked in a read-only source connection before destination disposal or drop. The real PostgreSQL regression retains an occupied destination sentinel for pre-146 and malformed sources, and checks connection cleanup. The source-equals-target case is also refused.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preflight every database before starting the backfill**

When `--all` encounters a later target without migration 146, or later discovers that a fork parent has a non-backfill identity, earlier targets have already committed new UUIDs in separate transactions before the command raises. This contradicts the function's stated pre-write refusal contract and leaves a partially backfilled fleet; inspect every target and fork parent, including tables, identities, origins, and existing lineage, before the first insert.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in f192fccd. A read-only preflight inspects every target and fork parent before any insert, including both tables, identity row counts, fork origins, existing lineage, self-parentage and conflicting requested parents. Nine real PostgreSQL refusal scenarios assert that an earlier target stays unminted. The docstring now accurately describes the remaining per-database transaction boundary.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Redact user-controlled mapping keys from validation locations**

When malformed configuration places a secret-shaped string in a valid mapping key—for example, a provider key under `[global.model.api_models]` with an invalid nested field—Pydantic includes that key in the middle of `error["loc"]`. This code redacts only the final component for `extra_forbidden`, while `_safe_token` preserves values such as `sk-...`, so the supposedly sanitized receipt can write the secret verbatim. Redact every user-controlled mapping-key component or retain only allowlisted schema field names.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in `9f728a2a`, retained at current head `cf61a440`: validation locations now follow the declared model schema and redact every user-controlled mapping key, including keys that resemble valid schema fields. `test_validation_receipt_redacts_identifier_mapping_keys` covers both a planted secret and `default_slot` through real invalid TOML; both cases failed before the fix and pass afterward. The focused runtime/config/CLI/document suite passed (588 passed, 18 PostgreSQL skips); receipt regressions and document freshness were rerun at exact implementation commit `9f728a2a` (58 passed). See [verification](https://github.com/pythagorakase/nexus/blob/cf61a440da7f3236226c717d031a493cbc25f5c5/docs/qa/806-receipt-store/verification.md).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Deduplicate coincident home and fallback receipt roots**

When `NEXUS_HOME` is the user's home directory, both roots resolve to `$HOME/.nexus/receipts`. Adding the same directory under two labels makes `_read_receipts` scan every file twice, doubling each group's count and falsely reporting both `home` and `fallback`; avoid adding the fallback root when it resolves to the home root.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed by the resolved-root comparison in `run_receipts`, retained at current head `cf61a440`: coincident home/fallback directories are scanned once. `test_home_equal_to_user_home_reads_each_receipt_once` exercises the subprocess CLI with `NEXUS_HOME=$HOME`, asserts one receipt/count and the single `fallback` label, and verifies the file is unchanged. The focused runtime/config/CLI/document suite passed (588 passed, 18 PostgreSQL skips); receipt regressions and document freshness were rerun at exact implementation commit `9f728a2a` (58 passed). See [verification](https://github.com/pythagorakase/nexus/blob/cf61a440da7f3236226c717d031a493cbc25f5c5/docs/qa/806-receipt-store/verification.md).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Translate receipt decoding failures into read errors**

If a receipt file contains invalid UTF-8—possible when `_append` leaves a short write ending midway through a Unicode path—decoding fails during stream iteration before `model_validate_json` enters its exception handler. The resulting `UnicodeDecodeError` bypasses `ReceiptReadError`, so `nexus receipts` emits a traceback rather than its documented `domain_failure`; catch decoding and file-read errors and wrap them with the receipt path and line context.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed at current head `cf61a440`: receipt files are read as bytes, invalid UTF-8 becomes a path-and-line `ReceiptReadError`, and filesystem read failures are wrapped too. `test_undecodable_receipt_line_is_a_read_error` verifies the subprocess `domain_failure` envelope and unchanged bytes; `test_unreadable_receipt_file_is_a_read_error` covers the filesystem failure. The focused runtime/config/CLI/document suite passed (588 passed, 18 PostgreSQL skips); receipt regressions and document freshness were rerun at exact implementation commit `9f728a2a` (58 passed). See [verification](https://github.com/pythagorakase/nexus/blob/cf61a440da7f3236226c717d031a493cbc25f5c5/docs/qa/806-receipt-store/verification.md).
